newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Parents of dead Belgian children raise pressure.
newsitem.headline: Parents of dead Belgian children raise pressure.

text.p: The parents of two of the children killed in Belgium's paedophile murder case, anxious to avoid investigations stalling, have called for the interior minister to quit and threatened a new mass rally.

It is the first time a serving minister has been threatened by the scandal, which broke three months ago with the arrest of rapist Marc Dutroux, the rescue of two sexually abused young girls and the discovery of the bodies of four more.

"I think the minister of the interior should resign," said Gino Russo, father of Melissa whose body was found buried alongside that of friend Julie Lejeune on a property owned by Dutroux near the central Belgian city of Charleroi.
"If he doesn't we will organise...a red march," Julie's father Denis told Belgian radio. Red symbolises anger.
Brussels was brought to a standstill last month when 250,000 people took to the streets in white to signify sympathy with the parents of the dead and missing girls.

Julie and Melissa's parents hold Interior Minister Johann Vande Lanotte responsible for the bungling, inefficiency and rivalry among the police -- and particularly the gendarmerie -- that has come to light during renewed inquiries.
But Vande Lanotte told RTBF television he refused to be a scapegoat, adding that it was Justice Minister Stefaan de Clerck who was politically responsible for the gendarmerie.

Allegations of a cover-up have been fuelled by the removal from the case last month of the magistrate leading the investigations, accused of having compromised himself by accepting a free pasta dinner from a parental support group.
The ruling by Belgium's highest court sparked demonstrations across the country and fired emotions at the white march.

The parents of the dead and some of the missing children have now decided to lodge a formal appeal against the decision to remove magistrate Jean-Marc Connerotte -- seen as one of the few honest magistrates in the country -- from the case.
The government has set up an enquiry into the earlier investigations and promised rapid reforms of the judicial system -- particularly over the political promotion of magistrates.
It is also looking at creating a Federal Bureau of Investigation to supplement the existing territorially and linguistically-divided police and gendarmerie forces.
A parliamentary enquiry has already begun hearing evidence from the families, the investigators, the police and magistrates involved in all the cases.
But investigations have been further complicated by the fact that Dutroux and his accomplices have also been linked to organised car theft and other criminal activity.

"We want to avoid all risks because we are certain that Marc Dutroux had or has links with banditry in and around Charleroi," Michel Bourlet, the public prosecutor in charge of the investigations, told Het Volk newspaper.
